runtime: Zero-build-step browser app. src/ imports bare specifiers (react, zustand, jszip, ...); a browser import map injected by index.html resolves them to either the esm.sh CDN or the local ./vendor/ folder, selectable at runtime (see offline_mode below).

module_resolution.mechanism: Browser import maps (<script type="importmap">), injected dynamically by an inline classic script in index.html before src/main.js loads.

modes.cdn: Bare specifiers resolve to pinned esm.sh URLs.
modes.vendor: Bare specifiers resolve to ./vendor/<name>.js, produced by requirements/vendor-deps.py (default - this folder ships with ./vendor/ already populated so it works with zero internet access out of the box).

module_resolution.toggle: Top-bar on-page control, or ?modules=cdn / ?modules=vendor in the URL (persisted to localStorage).

cdn_dependencies.name: htm
cdn_dependencies.purpose: JSX-like tagged templates without a compiler step

cdn_dependencies.name: zustand
cdn_dependencies.purpose: App state: networks, undo/redo history, UI selection

cdn_dependencies.name: fast-xml-parser
cdn_dependencies.purpose: Tolerant, comment-preserving XML <-> JS parsing/serialization of messy Sysmon configs (used in preserveOrder mode)

cdn_dependencies.name: jszip
cdn_dependencies.purpose: Bundles all exported network XML files into one .zip download

why_cdn_instead_of_npm: This environment has no Node.js/npm installed, so `npm install` + a bundler (Vite/webpack) cannot run here. Loading pinned-version ES modules directly from esm.sh gives the same package versions with zero install step and no local toolchain dependency, satisfying the brief's 'work seamlessly online via reliable CDNs' allowance.

offline_mode.description: Stdlib-only Python script that recursively crawls every import/export specifier starting from the 7 dependencies above (plus the Tailwind CDN script), mirrors each file under ./vendor/, and rewrites every internal import to a relative local path. Run once while online; the app can then run with zero internet access, verified by driving it in a browser with every non-localhost request blocked.

npm_equivalent.description: If Node.js becomes available, `npm install` using package.json's dependencies/devDependencies plus a Vite config will let the same src/ files run through a real bundler - src/ already imports bare package names, so no source changes are needed; just drop the import-map bootstrap from index.html since a bundler resolves bare specifiers itself.
